exercise.name: Walking
library_steps: Wear comfortable shoes and start at an easy pace.
Walk briskly, swinging your arms, until you breathe a little harder.
Slow down for the last few minutes.
exercise.one_line_summary: Walking on plain ground (no scenery drawn). Picture 1: left foot forward, right foot pushing off behind; picture 2: the other way round. Arms swing freely opposite to the legs.

movement.measure: knee bend at heel contact / flat foot

movement.start: heel up on the ball of the foot

muscles.emg: Vastii active at loading in level walking (S1).
muscles.role: Library primary 'cardio' has no mask; front thigh lit.

mistakes.why_it_matters: Arm swing is natural and steadies walking (S2).

sources.citation: Franz JR, Kram R. The effects of grade and speed on leg muscle activations during walking. Gait Posture. 2012;35(1):143-147.
sources.what_it_gave: Walking uphill at 9 deg: biceps femoris x6.4, gluteus maximus x3.5, vastus medialis x3.7 and medial gastrocnemius x1.75 compared with level walking.

sources.citation: Meyns P, Bruijn SM, Duysens J. The how and why of arm swing during human walking. Gait Posture. 2013;38(4):555-562.
sources.what_it_gave: Arms swing opposite to the legs in walking and running.

clip_check.target: heel up on the ball of the foot -> (other leg) (10-25 deg)
